correctness.rationale: For every fixed nonempty interval, the complement has two independent fair-Bernoulli increment strings. Repeated application of the SAME sampled map to distance h is exactly h -> S_(h-1), never a newly resampled binomial. A uniform simultaneous Chernoff–Hoeffding bound for all distances at least C loglog t sandwiches the farthest-tail absorption time between (log t)/log(1/(1/2-delta)) and (log t)/log(1/(1/2+delta)), up to o(log t), uniformly over tail lengths with sum t. Taking delta down to zero proves the conditional law. Existing exact fixed-point counts make n-|Fix(f)| asymptotic to n in probability, proving the unconditional law. Independent direct-composition exhaustive checks through n=10 agree with the separate prefix recursion. The finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The first repeated power at which an element reaches its idempotent limit is an intrinsic semigroup dynamical invariant. The result replaces a worst-case linear stabilization horizon by a sharp, universal leading logarithmic typical law. Its uniformity under arbitrary prescribed nonempty fixed intervals is a substantive strengthening and is not implied by the classical joint rank/fixed-point enumeration. A single exact infinite-family asymptotic theorem is meaningful without a further CLT or limiting additive fluctuation law.
